newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank to hold Zunk bond secondary auction.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank to hold Zunk bond secondary auction.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) will hold the first secondary auction on July 15 of two issues of bad debt bonds, known as Zunks, the BNB said in a statement.

Financial institutions have so far traded lev- and dollar denominated Zunks on bilateral basis. The Tuesday auction will trade issue 98/93, which is lev-denominated and its par value was 19.813 billion levs by end-May, said the statement.
The second issue, 97/94, is denominated in US dollars and its par stood at $917.6 million at end-May. The settlement for the auction is July 17, the BNB added.
Investors' interest in the bonds has been running high because the bonds are accepted as means of payment in local sell-offs.

Bulgaria's government scrapped last month minimum prices for Zunks, as part of pledges to free trade. Local banks now trade dollar-denominated ZUNKs at 65-72 percent of par. Lev-denominated bonds traded at 61-65 percent of par.
Only financial institutions that are primary dealers of government securities will be allowed to take part in the auction, the statement said.
Other companies, individuals and financial institutions may take part in the auction through orders placed with the primary dealers.
Participants in the auction can place only one order on their behalf and one order on behalf of their clients. They should also set a maximum buy price or a minimum sell price.
The Zunk auction sell offers are irrevocable, the BNB said.
According to the bids and offers placed, the central bank will set an equilibrium price, at which the deals will be struck, the statement said.
The BNB will inform the primary dealers on the buyer side for the auction results by the close of day on July 15.
